evidence: South Africa's first 2023 dashboard row (week 35: 1,390 cases, 47 deaths) is the year-to-date total of an outbreak the Department of Health (NDoH) dates from 1 February 2023 ('between 1st of February and 4 July 2023', media statement of 5 July; WHO's situation reports give 29/01/2023) and WHO AFRO's after-action review counts to 31 July (1,380 cases and 47 deaths by 31 July). Spread over the WHO weeks (Monday-Sunday) of 1 February to 31 July in proportion to dated curves (shape 'cumulative', anchors in surveillance_curation_shapes.csv, built by data-raw/make_surveillance_curation_shapes.R). Cases: WHO's epidemic curve by symptom onset (external situation report #5, Figure 5, as of 15 July), digitized: 1,271 cases, NDoH's 1,073 suspected and 198 confirmed of 4 July. WHO's other weekly rows are dated by report week and the model has one reporting delay for all locations, so the onset dates are moved 2 days later, the onset-to-notification lag at which the onset curve's cumulative shape best matches the notification-date curve of situation report #4 (Figure 2). The imported case of NDoH's statement of 25 July (symptoms 14 July after travel from Karachi, admitted 18 July, confirmed 24 July; the 199th confirmed case) is placed by the same rule on 16 July. The resulting 1,272 cases are scaled to the report's 1,390: WHO's count rose to 1,380 by 31 July while NDoH's stayed at 1,073 suspected and 199 confirmed, so the cases WHO added have no date and follow the curve. Weekly cases peak at 432 in 22-28 May. Deaths follow their own curve of report-dated national counts: the first death (Benoni) announced 23 February; 1 death as of 15 May (WHO situation report #3); the Gauteng Department of Health's Hammanskraal deaths plus the Benoni death, 11 as of 21 May, 16 on 22 May and 21 as of 24 May; the official national toll of 24 on 27 May; 25 on 28 May (the 23 Hammanskraal deaths, the Benoni death and the Free State death of 25 May at Parys hospital; the first Mpumalanga death came on 30 May); 31 as of 6 June (NDoH); 38 as of 15 June (WHO situation report #4); 43 at the 25 June report and 47 as of 4 July (NDoH, 5 July). WHO's 44 deaths as of 9 July (situation report #5) trails NDoH's 47 and is not used. The weeks from 17 July to the report carry 0.
reference: NDoH media statements of 5 July 2023 (https://www.health.gov.za/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Health-Department-provides-update-on-cholera-outbreak-in-SA-05-July-2023.pdf) and 25 July 2023 (https://www.health.gov.za/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Health-Minister-announces-another-imported-cholera-case-25-July-2023.pdf) ; WHO AFRO, Cholera Outbreak Response and After-Action Review (South Africa, 2023): https://www.afro.who.int/countries/south-africa/news/cholera-outbreak-response-and-after-action-review ; WHO, Multi-country outbreak of cholera, External situation reports #3 (1 June 2023), #4 (6 July 2023, Figure 2) and #5 (4 August 2023, Figure 5): https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-cholera--external-situation-report--5---4-august-2023 ; deaths: SAnews 26 February 2023 (https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/tracing-close-contacts-benoni-cholera-victim-underway), Inside Metros 22 May 2023 (https://insidemetros.co.za/2023/05/22/gauteng-health-mec-confirms-hammanskraal-cholera-outbreak-death-toll-at-10/), Daily Maverick 22 May 2023 (https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2023-05-22-cholera-death-toll-in-hammanskraal-rises-to-15-as-probe-yet-to-find-source-of-contaminated-water/), SAnews 25 May 2023 (https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/cholera-death-toll-rises-20), 29 May 2023 (https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/cholera-death-toll-climbs-23-hammanskraal), News24 25 May 2023 (https://www.news24.com/southafrica/news/cholera-outbreak-woman-dies-in-free-state-as-gauteng-death-toll-rises-to-20-20230525), The Citizen 27 May 2023 (https://www.citizen.co.za/news/cholera-death-toll-hammanskraal-tshwane-eastern-cape/), OFM 9 June 2023 (https://www.ofm.co.za/article/centralsa/326313/cholera-claimed-second-life-in-free-state) and 8 June 2023 (https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/cholera-death-toll-rises-31-sa-166-laboratory-confirmed-cases-recorded)

evidence: Namibia's first 2025 dashboard row (week 12: 22 cases) has no row before it and Namibia had no cholera from 2015 to 2024; the Ministry of Health and Social Services dates the first case to Sunday 2 March 2025 (a patient at Opuwo District Hospital, Kunene; stool sample collected 3 March, laboratory-confirmed 10 March).
